newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices track world market falls.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices track world market falls.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were lower on Thursday in line with overnight falls in New York and London futures, with local arrivals increasing as the main crop harvest gathers momentum, traders said.
Malaysian prices also weakened, with traders expecting local market activity to pick up only when values improve.

Indonesian traders said 4,000 tonnes of cocoa purchased by Brazilian companies awaited shipment at Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, and added that they were confident of more imports by the South American country.
One trader said he expected Brazilian companies to import another 8,000 tonnes.
Brazilian producers have endorsed purchases of up to 15,000 tonnes of cocoa until August to cover a shortfall in supply at the start of the local Bahian midcrop.
"Some players are taking the opportunity of the price declines in New York and London to buy beans," one trader said. "Others are buying to fill outstanding contracts."
"Local prices have fallen in line with the declines at the two terminals," he said. "Supply is beginning to increase steadily as the harvest continues."
Cocoa arrivals in Ujung Pandang were estimated at some 9,600 tonnes in March, up from about 3,000 tonnes in February, when the mid-crop harvest ground to a halt.
Traders said cocoa was quoted at 2,800-2,850 rupiah a kg in Ujung Pandang, down from 3,085-3,100 rupiah a week ago.
In New York, May slumped US$20 to close at $1,380 a tonne on Wednesday after ranging between $1,408 to $1,370.
The fall was attributed to speculators continuing to liquidate long positions and rolling May contracts forward ahead of the spot month's delivery period.
In London, May ended down two sterling at 970 stg a tonne on Wednesday while July was down seven at 980 stg after fund sales emerged in late trading.
Traders said they expected London to open unchanged to marginally higher later on Thursday.
"When the London market closed yesterday, New York's May was trading at $1,378 and closed $2 higher at $1,380. So I think London will open one sterling higher today," one trader said.
The Malaysian Cocoa Board quoted Standard Malaysian Cocoa (SMC) Grade 1A out of the main growing region of Tawau at an average 3,235 ringgit a tonne, down 75 ringgit from a week ago.
The board quoted the SMC 1B grade in Tawau at an average 3,185 ringgit, down 73 ringgit from last week.
Traders offered SMC 1A at 3,160 ringgit a tonne and SMC 1B at 3,260-3,270 ringgit.
"I don't see much local activity until the price goes up again," the commercial manager of a cocoa trading house in Malaysia said.
"I think the plantations will wait for the market to pick up before selling again," he said.
Traders said there will, however, be no squeeze on supplies as grinders and end-users were still comfortable with their bean stocks, sourced mostly from overseas.
"They (grinders) have not only been buying beans from Tawau but also from Indonesia and Ivory Coast, so supply's alright," a trader said.
